purpose: Fail-closed manufacture/install interface contract for the benchmark-close municipal slide. The prior generated slide had a roughly 2 m platform and chute but no climbable stair/access assembly and no explicit head/runout support path. This contract adds period-plausible stair geometry, side-stringer brackets, support interfaces and LOD requirements without awarding Visual Fidelity points from source evidence.

referenceBasis.topic: standard drawing for large playground slide SU-L
requirementsUsed: large slide includes an explicit stair/access section (階段) and platform
stair tread depth 170 mm or greater
sliding surface stainless plate 1.5 mm or greater
large-slide major steelwork is a separately supported fabricated assembly with dedicated ascent and landing foundations
referenceBasis.historicalContext: The Yokohama standard-drawing lineage listed in the same document includes partial revisions in April 1999 and April 2002. The 2018 sheet is therefore used as a construction-principle and safety-envelope reference, not as proof that every detail matches one exact circa-2000 manufacturer product.

referenceBasis.topic: fictional scene slide envelope and material classes
requirementsUsed: 2.0 mm modeled SUS304 sliding skin and side sheets
four LOD levels with animated cross-fade
generated visual shell adds no gameplay collider

assemblySequence: below-grade/foundation interface retained by existing gameplay ground
two inclined coated-steel side stringers outside the tread envelope
twenty welded tread-support brackets, one at each tread/stringer side interface
two coated-steel access handrails and platform transition rails
existing platform guard posts/top rail where retained by the source LOD, or dimension-matched generated transition guard at the coarsest LOD
existing coated-steel platform and support frame
coated-steel chute-head bearing crossmember tied back to the platform frame
existing continuous 2 mm SUS304 chute shell and raised side sheets
coated-steel runout bearing crossmember with two short support posts and foot plates
LOD0-only exposed fastener heads at the chute-head bearing interface
manufactureReconstruction.mounting: The access stair climbs from grade on local -Z to the rear edge of the existing platform. Horizontal treads do not slice through inclined round stringers: the stringers sit laterally outside the 780 mm tread width, and each tread seats on a pair of small welded support brackets whose outer ends intentionally overlap the stringer tube envelope. Stringers terminate into foot plates at grade and continue to the platform underside. Access handrails follow the stair pitch and bridge into the platform guard. Because the original coarse LOD omits that guard, the access pass restores dimension-matched transition posts/top rail in LOD3 so the stair cannot terminate into empty space or create a topology-scale temporal pop. The chute head bears on a transverse frame member linked to the existing support legs; the low runout bears on a transverse member with two short ground-supported posts.
manufactureReconstruction.interfacesAndSeals: No decorative sealant or painted contact shadow is permitted. Steel-to-steel weld/bracket joints may use millimetric intentional overlap. Positive daylight gaps between tread and bracket, bracket and stringer, stringer and foot plate, access handrail bridge and platform guard, chute and either bearing member, or top tread and platform access are source-side failures. The tread plate itself must retain positive lateral clearance from the inclined round stringer so a horizontal plate never unrealistically cuts through the pipe.
manufactureReconstruction.orientation: Local +Z is the descending chute direction. Access stairs rise toward local +Z from the rear at local -Z. Treads remain horizontal; stringers and handrails follow approximately 50.9 degrees above horizontal. Platform transition posts remain vertical and the top guard remains horizontal.
manufactureReconstruction.exposure: Tread tops, handrails and platform receive strong midsummer UV/rain and hand/foot contact. Brackets, stringer undersides and chute-head hardware are partially sheltered. Ground plates and runout supports receive splash and persistent near-grade contamination.
manufactureReconstruction.aging: Paint chalking follows UV exposure; handrails receive local polish; tread noses receive directional foot abrasion; near-grade plates receive splash darkening and restrained ferrous oxidation at real steel sources only. SUS304 travel abrasion follows the chute direction and is not represented as random rust.
manufactureReconstruction.geometryVsMaterialDetail: Tread count/depth/thickness, side stringers, welded tread brackets, rails, platform transition guard, foot plates, bearing crossmembers, posts and visible fastener heads are geometry. Checker-plate relief below silhouette scale, weld bead microrelief, paint orange-peel/chalking, fine abrasion, local polish, micro-rust and water residue are material/weathering detail.
manufactureReconstruction.lodPolicy: LOD0/1/2/3 all retain the ten-step stair silhouette, side stringers, tread-support brackets, access rails, platform transition guard continuity, head bearing and runout support to prevent topology-scale popping. LOD0-2 may join the original platform guard; LOD3 restores equivalent guard geometry because the source LOD omits it. Only LOD0 retains small chute-head fastener heads. All new renderers must be rebound into the corresponding existing HD_Slide LOD renderer set with animated cross-fade.

coatedStructuralSteel.microstructure: subtle baked/powder-coat orange peel and age-related chalking; checker tread and weld relief remain material-scale where below silhouette resolution
coatedStructuralSteel.uvAging: upward and sun-facing surfaces chalk/desaturate more strongly than sheltered undersides
coatedStructuralSteel.angularResponse: dielectric Fresnel from real sun/sky/probes; no painted highlight

exposedFastenerSteel.microstructure: fine galvanizing/machining and restrained oxidation variance
exposedFastenerSteel.angularResponse: metallic reflection from the actual environment

stainlessChute.microstructure: fine directional travel abrasion without painted specular streaks
stainlessChute.wetness: lower apparent roughness only when an explicit rain/wet state is active
stainlessChute.uvAging: no paint chalking; contamination and fine abrasion only
stainlessChute.angularResponse: strong grazing reflection driven by BRDF/Fresnel and real environment
